Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out there in the middle. Chad Bowes and Tim Seifert are the two openers for New Zealand. Kasun Rajitha to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Sri Lanka have posted a good total on the board and will be hoping their bowlers step up and defend this. New Zealand have some powerful strikers of the ball and they know that if they play the whole 20 overs, they can gun this down.

Kusal Mendis is in for a quick chat and says that he is delighted with his innings and he paced it well. He adds that the talk in between him and Pathum Nissanka was simple as they very planning to rotate the strike on a regular basis with boundaries on the loose deliveries and this paid well as the team has posted a brilliant total of 182 which seems really difficult to chase. He also adds that he has been loving his time in New Zealand and his daughter is in the crowd as well so the half-century feels an extra bit special to him.

The hosts, on the contrary, were poor in the field and that has cost them big. The bowlers bowled well but the batting was class by the Lankans. Benjamin Lister was brilliant as he scalped a couple while he was well helped by Adam Milne and Ish Sodhi who scalped a wicket each.

The visitors started off a bit cautiously as they were struggling to start with but once Daryl Mitchell dropped Kusal Perera the Lankan batters stepped up on the paddle and managed to smash the Kiwi bowlers all over the park. An opening partnership of 76 runs between Pathum Nissanka and Mendis laid a perfect platform for the others to come and have fun on. Mendis lived a charmed life as he was dropped later in his innings by Rachin Ravindra again but he eventually got out on a score of 73. Kusal Perera was good as well as he played a perfect cameo of 33 runs and continued to add trouble to the Kiwi camp. Dhananjaya de Silva also scored some quick runs, but they will be a bit disappointed with the last over as they only scored three runs which shifted the momentum a bit in the favour of the hosts.

We are halfway in the game as the Lankan innings end with 182 for the loss of 6 wickets. After being asked to bat first, Sri Lanka would be delighted with the score they have posted for the hosts to chase in the series decider.

Only a bye to end the innings them! Matt Henry sees the batter make room and serves this full and outside off, Wanindu Hasaranga is too far away from the ball, and tries to reach it, but misses and falls over too. However, the batters again get a bye run. Sri Lanka finish on 182/6!

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Chad Bowes, Tim Seifert, Tom Latham (C)&(WK), Daryl Mitchell, Mark Chapman, James Neesham, Rachin Ravindra, Adam Milne, Matt Henry (In for Henry Shipley), Ish Sodhi, Benjamin Lister.
TOSS- New Zealand has won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

New Zealand, on the other hand would be hoping to put up a performance as similar as they did in the second T20I, where they completely dominated the opponents and registered a series levelling victory. Their bowlers really did well and restricted the opponents to a below par total on a ground that had shorter boundaries. Tom Latham would be hoping that his bowlers give him exactly the same kind of performance and the way the batters batted while chasing the total and managed to chase that down without any hiccups. Adam Milne would lead the charge in the bowling department and a similar kind of performance would be required of him if his team is to register a second victory in the three match T20I series and clinch the silverware. The batting department would be dependent on Tim Seifert and Chad Bowes, along with the experienced Daryl Mitchell. It is going to be an exciting game of cricket. Stay tuned for toss up and team updates.

Sri Lanka started the series with the bang as they defeated the hosts in a thrilling game but were dominated in the second game against the Kiwis. The batters led the visitors down in the second game and if they are to clinch the series the batters will have to join the party and the bowlers too will have to play their part. A lot would depend on Kusal Mendis and Kusal Perera who have shown some fight so far. The bowling would depend on the broad shoulders of Maheesh Theekshana and Wanindu Hasaranga. They will take some points from both games and try to rectify their misttto win this game and the series.

Hello and welcome, to all our viewers. New Zealand takes on Sri Lanka for the third and final T20I at the beautiful John Davies Oval in Queenstown which is holding its first ever T20I with the series hanging in balance level at one each in the series decider.
